On Oct 12, 2022 the UN General Assembly voted on whether Russia's annexation of four Ukrainian regions had any legal validity. 143 countries said no. Five said yes. The interesting part of the map is the orange.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The resolution was ES-11/4. It condemned the “referendums” staged in Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia between Sept 23-27, 2022, and declared the attempted annexation that followed to have no legal validity whatsoever.

2/ Final tally: 143 in favour, 5 against, 35 abstentions, 10 not voting. That was more support than the resolution condemning the invasion itself had drawn seven months earlier, which passed 141-5-35.
3/ The five against were Russia, Belarus, North Korea, Syria and Nicaragua — the same five that had voted against in March. Subtract Russia's landmass and the red on this map nearly disappears.
4/ The abstentions are the story. China, India, Pakistan, South Africa and much of Central Asia sat it out — a bloc containing a large share of humanity that declined to call the annexation illegal.

5/ Abstaining wasn't endorsing. Several of those states said publicly they respected Ukraine's territorial integrity while opposing further isolation of Russia. Others had grain, debt, energy or arms dependencies to weigh.

6/ General Assembly resolutions aren't binding. No sanctions follow, no borders move. What they produce is a record — a snapshot of who was willing to say the words out loud in October 2022.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
